brief.outcome: Cut the month-end close at a 60-person distribution company from about 15 working days to 5 working days by March, with no errors in the board pack and nothing posted to the ledger without the finance manager's approval.

ambition.goal_beyond: The owner and board see reliable numbers within a week of month-end, and the finance team of two keeps it that way without heroics
rungs: Cut days off the slowest close tasks (bank reconciliations and accruals)
Redesign the close around its longest chain of tasks: reconcile through the month, a standard accrual schedule, inventory tied out on a fixed day, a board pack that ties to Xero
Keep the close at 5 days: a scorecard after each close that flags slipping days, late entries and post-close adjustments before they cost a week
ambition.judge: Xero's own history for working days from month-end to the period lock date and for journals dated into a locked period afterwards; the board pack totals tied line by line to Xero's trial balance by the finance manager; the bank statement balances for the three accounts against Xero's reconciliation report

research.approach: Practitioners shorten a close by finding its critical path rather than speeding every task. They time the last closes task by task, then fix the long chain: reconcile bank and payment accounts during the month with bank rules and suggested matches, so month-end only has exceptions; put accruals and prepayments on a standard schedule with recurring and reversing journals; tie sub-ledgers such as inventory out on a fixed day; and run a close calendar with owners, cut-off dates, dependencies and a named reviewer. They separate preparer from approver, attach support to every journal and reconciliation, and lock the period once approved. Published benchmarks put top performers at about 5 calendar days and small teams often near 14, so a 5 working-day close for a two-person team is a stretch that needs both the redesign and continuous reconciliation. The result is judged on a scorecard each month, not once.

sources.title: Xero guide: month-end close process
sources.note: Recommended order: code and reconcile bank accounts in days 1-2, reconcile payables and receivables, post accruals and prepayments (note which reverse), review, then lock the period on day 5. Keep a living checklist and a close calendar with cut-offs; reviewer separate from preparer; attach support.

sources.title: Rand Group: how long should month-end close take
sources.note: Benchmarks: APQC top performers 5 calendar days or less, median 6, bottom 10 or more. Red flags: heavy spreadsheets, manual exports, disconnected systems. Practices: close calendar, reconcile through the month, standardise reconciliations and accruals, automate recurring entries.

sources.title: Numeric: month-end close benchmarks
sources.note: Updated 2026-07-16. Small teams often take about 14 days; account reconciliations are the most time-consuming task; aim for 5 to 7 calendar days if not under public reporting rules.

sources.title: Xero: bank reconciliation
sources.note: Accessed 2026-11-03. Bank rules treat similar transactions the same way each time; Xero suggests matches from history; similar transactions can be grouped and cash coding shows up to 200 lines in a spreadsheet view (plan-dependent).

steps.why: The longest chain of dependent tasks sets the close time; the owner's 15 days is an estimate until timed.

steps.name: Check the books before redesigning: bank, Stripe, inventory
steps.why: Backlogs and unexplained differences make every later task longer and the board pack unsafe.

steps.name: Check who can post and lock in Xero
steps.why: The rule that nothing posts without the finance manager must hold in the system, not just in practice.

steps.name: Test why each task is slow and rank the redesign
steps.why: Reconciliations, accruals, inventory and board-pack rework each have a different fix.

steps.name: Move reconciliation into the month with rules and matches
Put accruals and inventory on a standard schedule
steps.why: Standard schedules with reversing entries turn a long judgement task into a short review.

steps.name: Build the close calendar, cut-offs and review steps
steps.why: Owners, dates and dependencies stop waiting time.

steps.name: Run a real close with every posting approved, then score it
steps.why: A trial on a live month shows what the plan missed; a scorecard keeps the gain.

pitfalls.text: Automating a task that is not on the critical path while the real delay (unreconciled backlog, inventory rec starting late) stays.
Posting accrual and rule changes in bulk without a reviewer, which breaks the owner's approval rule.
Bank rules set up wrongly, miscoding transactions that then pass reconciliation.
Locking the period before the board pack is tied out, then needing to unlock for corrections.
Judging success by one fast close rather than several in a row.

hypotheses.statement: The bank reconciliation backlog at month-end is the critical path.
hypotheses.test: Count and age unreconciled lines at month-end for the three accounts; hours spent on reconciliation in the timeline.
hypotheses.confirm_if: More than 5% of the month's bank lines are unreconciled at month-end, or reconciliation takes 5 or more of the 15 days.
hypotheses.refute_if: Under 1% unreconciled and reconciliation finishes by day 3.

hypotheses.statement: Stripe payouts, fees and refunds do not match the bank lines cleanly, so they pile up.
hypotheses.test: Stripe clearing account balance at month-end against Stripe's balance; unmatched payout lines.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The clearing account differs from Stripe's balance by more than 1% of the month's Stripe volume.
hypotheses.refute_if: The difference is under 0.1% and payouts match one-to-one.

hypotheses.statement: Spreadsheet accruals have no standard schedule, take days and are re-keyed.
hypotheses.test: Time spent on accruals in the timeline; whether each accrual has support and a reversing flag; last month's reversals against the sheet.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Accruals take 2 or more days, or any accrual lacks support or the reversal does not match, by more than 1% of the accrual balance.
hypotheses.refute_if: Accruals take under half a day and reverse correctly.

hypotheses.statement: The manual inventory reconciliation starts late and runs in series with other tasks.
hypotheses.test: Start date and duration of the inventory tie-out; gap between the inventory system and the Xero account.
hypotheses.confirm_if: It starts after working day 7, or takes 3 or more days, or the gap is over 1% of the inventory balance.
hypotheses.refute_if: It starts by day 2 and finishes in under 1 day with a gap under 0.5%.

hypotheses.statement: Tasks wait on each other without a real dependency because cut-offs and owners are not set.
hypotheses.test: The 'waiting for' column in the timeline; whether each dependency is real.
hypotheses.confirm_if: At least 3 tasks on the critical path wait without a data dependency.

hypotheses.statement: Late bills and expense claims keep the books open.
hypotheses.test: Share of the month's bills and claims entered after working day 3.
hypotheses.confirm_if: More than 20% of the month's bills or claims are entered after day 3.

hypotheses.statement: Board pack rework is a large part of the close.
hypotheses.test: Rounds of review and manual re-keying for the last pack; figures that did not tie on first pass.
hypotheses.confirm_if: More than one review round, or any figure that did not tie on first pass.
hypotheses.refute_if: One review round and every figure ties.

hypotheses.statement: Even with a redesign, a two-person team cannot do the work in 5 days.
hypotheses.test: Person-days needed after the supported changes against 10 person-days available.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The redesigned close needs more than 10 person-days.

hypotheses.statement: The close is not really 15 working days.
hypotheses.test: Compare the timed timeline with the owner's estimate.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The timed days differ from 15 by more than 20%.
hypotheses.refute_if: The timed days are within 3 of 15.

measurement.window: The next three month-end closes after the playbook goes live; each close is measured from the last day of the month to the lock date.
measurement.min_volume: Two consecutive closes at 5 working days or fewer before the target is called met; a single close is reported as one data point.
measurement.stop_rule: Stop adding changes and undo the last one if a close runs more than 2 days over its plan, or any board pack figure fails to tie; never lower the posting approval rule.
